source_name: LinkedIn Pulse / long-form posts by Hungarian fintech figures
why_relevant: Self-published Hungarian long-form on the fintech sector maps companies, founders and career histories — a rich actor-map and alias source, and its comment threads reveal who is currently where.

source_name: Év Bankja award results coverage – Portfolio / HVG / Pénzcentrum / Világgazdaság / Növekedés / Bank360 / Kreatív
why_relevant: Award-night reporting names the executives who accepted each prize and quotes them with current titles, and 'Az Év Bankára' (Banker of the Year) coverage identifies the individual singled out. This is often the only public place where a specific product/segment owner is attached to a named person.

source_name: Portfolio.hu / Economx – national wage bargaining (VKF) and banking sector coverage
why_relevant: Tracks the national wage bargain (VKF) rounds that set the envelope for bank-level collective agreements; Economx reported new bargaining rounds starting September 2026. Portfolio also covers bank governance/conduct and restructuring.

source_name: Blockchain Koalíció (state-initiated coalition, chaired by Vágujhelyi Ferenc)
why_relevant: Formed 8 March 2022 on the initiative of the innovation ministry and the national data-economy knowledge centre; its chairmanship links state digitalisation bodies to payments/DLT industry actors. Currently only reachable through trade-press coverage — a quasi-official body without an obvious standalone portal, so the interview article is the anchor for further tracing.

source_name: KiberPajzs consortium (MNB + Magyar Bankszövetség + NMHH + NBSZ-NKI + ORFK)
why_relevant: A standing cross-institutional programme (agreed 7 Nov 2022) whose signatories and spokespeople are named — it maps which institution owns financial-cybercrime/payments-fraud policy and who represents each. Institution-change and representative-change signals appear in its joint communiqués.

source_name: MBH Bank organigram (PDF org chart, deputy-CEO areas)
why_relevant: A published organisation chart mapping deputy-CEO areas — the single most valuable artefact for the 'organization changes' topic, because successive versions reveal restructurings directly. The observed file is dated 2023-05-01, so a newer revision is likely at a similar path.

source_name: OTP Bank – Közgyűlési dokumentumok és határozatok (AGM documents)
why_relevant: AGM proposals and resolutions state elections, re-elections and terminations of igazgatóság/felügyelőbizottság/audit bizottság members with exact effective dates — the crispest primary record of board-level leadership moves, published before annual reports.

source_name: Fintech.hu event reporting (Budapest Fintech Week etc.)
why_relevant: Covers the CEE-wide Budapest Fintech Week and panel line-ups, attaching regional fintech and bank leaders to current roles; complements FinTechZone with startup-side and cross-border titles.

source_name: MFB Zrt. — Alapszabály / corporate governance disclosures
why_relevant: State development bank publishes its statutes and governance documents defining board composition and appointment authority; combined with its BÉT bond-issuer disclosures it makes MFB's board changes fully traceable. Template for the other state-owned institutions (EXIM, MEHIB).

source_name: Hays Hungary Salary Guide 2026 — full PDF (Pénzcentrum CDN mirror)
why_relevant: An apparently ungated PDF copy of the full 2026 Hays Hungary salary guide hosted by a Hungarian business news site — the fastest route to the actual numeric salary tables (including finance/banking roles) without passing Hays' lead-capture gate.

source_name: Pénzcentrum – bank branch closure coverage
why_relevant: Consumer-finance outlet that reports named branch closure waves (MBH's post-merger network cuts: ~60 branches in one year, 360+ since the Budapest Bank/MKB/Takarekbank merger). Useful for dating and localising closures.

source_name: 424/2017. (XII. 19.) Korm. rendelet on electronic public procurement (Jogtár)
why_relevant: Defines what must be published where in EKR and the Közbeszerzési Értesítő, and the exemptions. Reading it tells the collection design which state-entity contracts are guaranteed to be visible and which are legally allowed to stay dark — essential for interpreting silence.

source_name: Corvinus Tehetségprogram regulation (BCE rule repository on net.jogtar.hu)
why_relevant: The formal internal regulation of Corvinus' talent programme; documents structure, corporate-partner modules and diploma-supplement recognition. Provides the vocabulary and programme architecture needed to interpret bank–university partnership announcements correctly.

source_name: Daily News Hungary – English-language coverage of Revolut HU expansion
why_relevant: English-language HU outlet reporting Revolut's local-branch build-out and hiring, including the MNB's push for a subsidiary and Revolut's decision against it — an entity-structure signal that directly shapes what and whom it hires in Hungary.

source_name: Forbes.hu – Revolut Hungary leadership coverage (Petrás Gábor appointment)
why_relevant: Forbes.hu broke the Revolut HU country-lead appointment (Petrás Gábor, Feb 2026) and the preceding vacancy after Tamás Léder's departure, with interim cover by Eduardo Pérez Toribio. Forbes.hu is a reliable HU outlet for named fintech CxO moves and profiles.

source_name: Index.hu – gazdaság / belföld banking labour and operations coverage
why_relevant: Mainstream outlet that covers finance-sector unionisation and bank operational disruptions; carried both the historical 'finance workers unionise' story and the 2026 UniCredit union-president dismissal with named counsel and the legal issue in dispute (business-secret rules).

source_name: mfor.hu / Privátbankár branch-network and headcount survey series
why_relevant: Runs a recurring bank-by-bank survey of branch counts and employee numbers, including the important counter-signal that branch closures in Hungary have NOT been accompanied by headcount reduction (sector employment rose past 40,500 by March 2026). Directly tests the assumption behind this cell.

source_name: SimplePay – corporate news / press releases
why_relevant: SimplePay's own announcement stream carried the legal-form and brand change (OTP Mobil Kft. -> SimplePay Zrt.) together with the CEO appointment (Bese Péter as vezérigazgató and OTP Bank merchant-services head) — exactly the org-change + leadership-move signal class this workstream tracks.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — Hungary banking & finance coverage and comparative guides
why_relevant: English CEE professional-services outlet; tracks lateral moves of banking/finance practice heads and in-house counsel, which are early indicators of institutional reorganisations and deal-team build-ups in Hungarian banks.

source_name: DigitalHungary – executive interviews (PayU Magyarország)
why_relevant: Interview-format outlet that names and profiles PSP managing directors (e.g. Váradi János, ügyvezető igazgató of PayU Magyarország, with prior Citibank/K&H background). Interviews and conference speaker lists are a reliable way to confirm who currently holds a role when no press release exists.

entity_name: Employment-law practitioner commentary on collective redundancy
source_name: Employment-law practitioner commentary on collective redundancy (arsboni, drujvary, Jogkövető iratminták)
why_relevant: Explains the Hungarian thresholds, timelines, works-council (üzemi tanács) consultation duty and the mandatory authority notification — necessary to know exactly what documentary artefacts a given bank cut must generate and when. Jogkövető publishes the actual works-council notification template.

source_name: EY Hungary – pay transparency and worker-representative consultation guidance
why_relevant: Maps the new/expanding consultation obligations toward worker representatives in Hungary — an emerging source of disclosure duties that will generate additional documentary traces around restructuring and pay in banks.

source_name: Gránit Bank Nyrt. – éves jelentés (issuer PDF, also mirrored by MBH Befektetési Bank)
why_relevant: Fast-growing HU digital bank, newly listed; its annual report carries board composition and headcount, and growth-phase hiring shows up as headcount step-changes in the filed accounts. Also demonstrates that third-party investment-bank sites mirror issuer annual reports — a useful redundancy path.

entity_name: Hungarian general/business media covering payment-infrastructure operators
source_name: Hungarian general/business media covering payment-infrastructure operators (Origo, Kisalföld, Pénzcentrum, Magyar Nemzet)
why_relevant: Mainstream HU outlets cover ATM deployers and payment operators from a consumer angle (fees, estate size) and also report executive appointments at state-linked financial bodies; they provide corroboration and occasionally the only public trace of an operational change.

source_name: Marketing.hu – Karrier rovat (appointment announcements)
why_relevant: Its 'karrier' section is a dedicated Hungarian appointment-announcement channel (carried the Fintech Association presidency change). Companies routinely push CxO/appointment PR here, so it catches moves that never appear in finance media.

source_name: money.hu tudástár – banking network statistics reporting
why_relevant: Publishes quantified branch-count time series (1401 branches at start of 2025 → 1300 at year end → 1268 at 31 March 2026), i.e. a ready-made derived indicator of network contraction with quarterly granularity.

source_name: Simple.hu – consumer-brand newsroom (OTP group payments)
why_relevant: Consumer-facing sister domain of the same issuer; duplicates and sometimes precedes corporate announcements, useful as a redundancy channel when simplepay.hu is restructured.
